_comment: Baseline numbers for bin/bench.sh.  Each scenario gets two floors
(mars_parse_MBps and mars_live_MBps) plus a vs-best-other ratio.
If a current measurement falls below the floor, the gate fails.
Tolerances bake observed run-to-run noise (~5% headless, ~10% live)
into the floor so the gate doesn't flap on identical code.
you actually want to lock in.  Re-run cross-terminal numbers via
`bin/measure-other.sh` if the iTerm2 / Warp comparison drifts.
Numbers below were locked in 2026-05-03 against:
- iTerm2 / Warp = whatever was installed on the user's machine

render_full_repaint._comment: p99 across 1000 iterations × median of 3 trials.  Real-world swing on a hot mac is up to ~2 ms; ceiling at 1.8 ms catches an actual regression while tolerating thermal/scheduler noise.

binary_size_bytes_max._comment: Release binary size ceiling (after lto=fat strip).  Used to flag accidental code-size growth (e.g. forgetting #[inline] removals, or pulling in a heavy dep).  10% headroom over current (794 KiB after metal-perf adds the offscreen Metal bench harness).

memory_idle_kb_max._comment: RSS in KiB, sampled 1.5 s after launch with no input.  Lazy-alloc scrollback ring (commit landed in this branch) means idle pays only for sessions' immediate state, not the worst-case 19 MiB ring.  20 % headroom over current.

competitors_snapshot._comment: Last cross-terminal observation, used to compute mars_vs_best_other.  Refresh by running bin/measure-other.sh and updating these.
